channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: Keep Unreal Engine 5 Projects Clean with This Optimization Toolkit
item.description: Leartes Studios' editor extension scores project health, finds unused assets and maps dependencies, helping Unreal Engine 5 developers keep their projects tidy.

item.title: Say cheese! Recreating an iconic 2D art style with UE5 in Bluey's Happy Snaps
item.description: The Gameloft Brisbane team shares how Unreal Engine 5 animation tools helped translate the hit kids' TV show Bluey's iconic 2D world into a 3D game.

item.title: The Unity CLI 1.0 is here!
item.description: Unity's command-line tool is out of beta, letting developers connect Claude Code and other AI coding assistants to a Unity project and automate builds and tests from the terminal.

item.title: 62 tiny browser games and counting: Pop Recall's daily shipping log
item.description: Pop Recall launched four days ago with 25 tiny browser games in vanilla JavaScript and has already grown to 62, still shipping daily; every new game must pass the same ship gates — a real win state, mobile widths, a pause that actually locks input — and gets live-checked after deploy.

item.title: Building a Real-Time Multiplayer Board Game Engine with HTML5 Canvas & WebSockets: The Architecture of Ludo Classic
item.description: The author breaks down the architecture of a real-time multiplayer board game engine, showing how HTML5 Canvas rendering and WebSocket sync power turn-based play.

item.title: I built an AI agent that edits Unreal Engine Blueprints from a chat prompt
item.description: A solo dev spent a year building Dola AI, an assistant inside Unreal Engine 5 that turns plain-language requests into Blueprint edits, C++ code and automated playtests — the post explains how it works and where it still falls short.

item.title: Indie Devs Push Back as Publisher Demands 55% Revenue Without Guaranteeing Marketing Spend
item.description: A pinball roguelike from five Finnish students drew a first publishing offer taking 55% of revenue with no marketing guarantee, sparking debate among peers over what counts as a fair publishing split.

item.title: Newzoo: GTA 6 pre-orders are archetypal console players but overwhelmingly male; game will "grow the market rather than simply redistribute it"
item.description: Newzoo data shows GTA 6 pre-orders come mostly from high-spending archetypal console players, overwhelmingly male, suggesting the game is likely to grow the overall market rather than merely redistribute existing players.

item.title: Best AI GIF Generators with Transparent Background (2026 Engineering Comparison)
item.description: Most AI animation tools output opaque rectangular video that still needs background removal; this comparison tests which generators produce transparent-background GIFs directly, saving creators the extra cleanup step.

item.title: The GTA VI Launch Engineering
item.description: Twenty-five million players pulling 150GB at roughly the same time is an extraordinary launch-day load; this technical walkthrough looks at the engineering behind surviving that download surge.

item.title: GDC survey: 70% of mobile studio workers use generative AI
item.description: A GDC survey of more than 2,600 industry professionals across 69 countries finds 70% of workers at mobile-only studios use generative AI, well above the industry average.

item.title: Football Manager Fought Through Two Rough Years and Is Finally Back on Track
item.description: After switching to Unity, a cancelled FM25 and a rocky FM26, a conversation with the FM27 team on how the series is finding its footing again.

item.title: PixiJS Moves Into 3D – PixiJS 3D
item.description: PixiJS, the popular 2D WebGL and WebGPU framework, has moved into 3D, opening it up to developers using engines like GDevelop and RPG Maker.

item.title: NO AI Looking for a small team to help develop an existing Unreal Engine game
item.description: An indie developer who has spent about a year on a third-person action roguelite in Unreal Engine is looking for a small team to help take the game to its next stage.

item.title: Monster Hunter Outlanders passes $10.2 million in IAP revenue in two weeks
item.description: The Monster Hunter mobile spin-off passed $10.2 million in in-app purchase revenue in just over two weeks — a handy benchmark for indie developers weighing mobile monetization.

item.title: How to Make a Game with AI, From the Idea to Your Phone
item.description: Describe your idea in a sentence, review the plan the AI writes, play the build on your phone, then tune it by telling the AI what to change — this guide walks first-time makers through the full AI game-making loop with the Tyrbo engine, and flags the mistakes that cost beginners the most.

item.title: Sensor Tower: GTA 6 pre-orders exceed $1.4bn, with 87% for the Ultimate Edition
item.description: Pre-order figures show how readily players accept premium editions — a useful signal for pricing and edition strategy on big-budget releases.

item.title: Foreign Media Hype: The US Has Lost Control of the Global Mobile Game Market, China Has Taken Its Place!
item.description: The article looks at how Chinese developers secured their place on global mobile bestseller charts and what the shift in market leadership means for the industry.

item.title: A Cert-Week Regression Set for PS5, Xbox and Nintendo Switch Submissions
item.description: A repeatable regression checklist built around what Sony's TRC, Microsoft's XRs and Nintendo's Lotcheck have in common, so submission week becomes confirmation rather than discovery.

item.title: Interview with the ARC Raiders Producer: Developed Without a Design Doc, Then a Divided Player Base After the Breakout
item.description: Embark's team discusses developing ARC Raiders without a design document, and how its breakout success was followed by a divided player base and repeated crises.
